outputs.exact_statement:
Fix $s\in(0,1]$ and $0<c<1/(4\log2)$. Along every sequence of instances $(n,q)$ with $n\to\infty$, $q\in(0,1)$, and $q^3\log n\to\infty$, $$\label{eq:main-bound}
 T_{q,s}(n)\ge n^{c\log(q^3\log n)}$$ eventually. All logarithms are natural. In particular, for each fixed deletion probability $q\in(0,1)$ and fixed positive success probability $s$, the required sample number is $n^{\Omega(\log\log n)}$.

Fix $B,\zeta,c_+$ and the parameters of this section. Along every sequence with $n\to\infty$ and $\delta^3\log n\to\infty$, for all sufficiently large instances there exist level-$i$ pairs satisfying Definition 4 simultaneously for $0\le i\le D$. The choices of $C,\omega$ depend only on $\delta$ and obey the displayed logarithmic bounds, and one $M_B$ depending only on $B$ works at every level.

Let $w$ be a nonempty word, $k$ a positive integer, and $0<\omega<1/8$ such that $\mathop{\mathrm{ov}}(\mathrm{Tr}(w^k),\mathrm{Tr}(w^{k+1}))\ge\omega$. There is an absolute constant $C_{\rm abs}$ such that, whenever $C\ge C_{\rm abs}/\omega$, $P$ is a sufficiently large positive integer, and the integer $F$ satisfies $F\ge CkP$, we have $$\label{eq:lift}
\mathop{\mathrm{ov}}(\mathrm{Tr}(w^{FP}),\mathrm{Tr}(w^{FP+P}))\ge 2/3.$$ It is enough that $P$ exceed an absolute constant, uniformly in $w,k,\omega,C,F$.

Fix a level $0\le i\le D$ and its parameters from Section 2. Suppose preliminary oracle laws have common “side” metadata with law $Q_{ m side}$, and conditional densities $G_x,G_y$ over a conditional reference $Q$, possibly depending on metadata. Require $\int G_x\,dQ=\int G_y\,dQ=1$ for $Q_{ m side}$-almost every metadata value. Use $Q_{ m side}Q$ as the joint reference. Suppose on a typical metadata event of probability $\ge1-o(\Delta)$ we have uniform estimates $$\label{eq:clipcond} \|G_x-1\|_{r_i},\|G_y-1\|_{r_i}\le N_i^{- ho}, \qquad \|G_y-G_x\|_{r_i}^2\le N_i^{-d_i-.01}$$ in $L^{r_i}(Q)$, where $ ho\ge 2^{-4B-10}$. Then conditioning each law on the event consisting of typical metadata and $G_x\ge1/2$ changes it in total variation by $o(\Delta)$. The conditioned laws $\mu, u$ satisfy $ u\ll\mu$ and $$\|d u/d\mu-1\|_{L^{r_i}(\mu)}^2\le N_i^{-d_i}.$$ All these conclusions hold uniformly over $0\le i\le D$.

For the parameters of Section 2, there is a choice of the common constants in Definition 4 with $M_B=1$ for which a level-zero pair exists with simulation error $E_0\le\Delta$. One may choose $\omega=\exp(-C_9\Lambda)$ for an absolute constant $C_9$, and $C>2$ with $\log C=O(\Lambda)$.

For fixed $1\le r<R_0$, uniformly in $h$ and $j\in[K/3,2K/3]$, $$\label{eq:base-fixed-sums}
 \Sigma_{r,h}(j)\le C_r(Km)^{-1/2}\lambda^{r-1},\qquad
 \Sigma_{r,h}^{\rm bd}(j)
 \le C_{r,s_0}(Km)^{-1/2}m^{-1/2}\lambda^{r-2}\quad(r\ge2).$$

For the parameters of Section 2, let $1\le i\le D$ and suppose a level-$(i-1)$ pair satisfies Definition 4 with constants $C,\omega,M_B$. Set $$C'=\max\{C,C_{\rm abs}/\omega\}.$$ The input pair remains valid when $C$ is replaced by $C'$, and there exists a level-$i$ pair satisfying the definition with the same constants $C',\omega,M_B$, with $$d_i=d_{i-1}+(b_i-1)/4-.05, \qquad E_i\le\Delta+(\ell_i/\ell_{i-1})E_{i-1}.$$ Every preceding level constructed with $C$ also remains valid with $C'$, and this enlarged value is retained in later blocks. The conclusion is uniform over all levels along the stated joint asymptotic regime.

Let $\sigma$ be the Prouhet–Thue–Morse sequence of order $s_*$ above. Suppose $\pi$ is an integer translation or reflection of a fair binomial probability mass function with $g\ge c_0\omega^2m$ trials, where $c_0>0$ is absolute and $m\to\infty$ as in the construction. Then $$\begin{aligned}
 \|\sigma*\pi\|_\infty
 &\le \exp(O((s_*+1)^2+(s_*+1)\Lambda))\,
       m^{-(s_*+1)/2},\nonumber\\
 \|\sigma*\pi\|_2^2
 &\le \exp(O((s_*+1)^2+(s_*+1)\Lambda))\,
       m^{-s_*-1/2},\qquad
 \|\pi\|_\infty\le O(\omega^{-1}m^{-1/2}).\label{eq:sig_conv}
\end{aligned}$$ The norms use counting measure on the integers, and the implicit constants may depend on $c_0$.

Under the input hypotheses of Proposition 13, the words and counts constructed above satisfy, for every $1\le j\le b$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{ov}}\bigl(\mathrm{Tr}((U_j^+)^{h_j}),\mathrm{Tr}((U_j^+)^{h_j+1})\bigr)\ge\omega.$$

For the unconditioned surrogate laws and the common projection above, $$\label{eq:projection_tree}
\begin{aligned}
 \mathop{\mathrm{TV}}(\mathcal K_{\rm tree}\widetilde\mu_i,\mathrm{Tr}(U_b^+))
 &\le o(\Delta)+\left(\prod_{j=1}^bT_j\right)E_{i-1},\\
 \mathop{\mathrm{TV}}(\mathcal K_{\rm tree}\widetilde\nu_i,\mathrm{Tr}(U_b^-))
 &\le o(\Delta)+\left(\prod_{j=1}^bT_j\right)E_{i-1}.
\end{aligned}$$ All error terms are uniform in $i$.

For every exact typical metadata value $\mathfrak d$, the densities in [eq:conditional-densities] satisfy $$\|G_+-G_-\|_{L^{r_i}(Q)}^2\le N^{-d'-.01}.$$ The bound is uniform in $\mathfrak d$ and the block level $i$.

evidence.quote: Let an explicitly listed finite directed acyclic graph specify the precedence constraints on $n\ge1$ nonpreemptive unit-length jobs on three identical machines. There is a uniform deterministic algorithm that constructs a feasible schedule of minimum makespan. Given also an integer deadline $1\le T\le n$, it decides feasibility exactly and returns a schedule whenever the answer is affirmative. Both tasks can be performed in $O((L+2)^{150020})$ steps on a deterministic multitape Turing machine, where $L$ is the total binary input length.

exclusions.query: Variable processing times or preemptible work
exclusions.reason: The result assumes nonpreemptive unit-length jobs.

hypotheses.statement: Let an explicitly listed finite directed acyclic graph specify the precedence constraints on $n\ge1$ nonpreemptive unit-length jobs on three identical machines. There is a uniform deterministic algorithm that constructs a feasible schedule of minimum makespan. Given also an integer deadline $1\le T\le n$, it decides feasibility exactly and returns a schedule whenever the answer is affirmative. Both tasks can be performed in $O((L+2)^{150020})$ steps on a deterministic multitape Turing machine, where $L$ is the total binary input length.
The original deadline is feasible if and only if $J$ has a full schedule. The padded instance has polynomial size in the stated input encoding.
Replacing the schedule inside an open interval by any full schedule of its job set preserves feasibility of the complete schedule.
The family $\mathcal F$ can be generated deterministically in polynomial time and represented by $N$-bit vectors.

This is a uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithm. Every set it accepts has a full schedule, which the algorithm can explicitly return. With $K=10000$, its deadline decision and schedule construction take $O((L+2)^{150020})$ deterministic multitape steps.
If a feasible $J$ has a bounded-description hierarchy, the algorithm accepts $J$.
Every feasible full three-machine schedule has a bounded-description hierarchy. In fact, the global node predicates and relative split predicates needed in the hierarchy have fewer than $500$ leaves.

If $z$ is an actual separator for a domain $U$ at cutoff $S$, and $H\cap U=S$, then $B_z(H)\cap U$ is exactly the set of domain jobs strictly earlier than $z$. Reversing order and time, and exchanging low with high, preserves the separator property.

In a normalized schedule, a feasible exchange that puts a better-priority job into an earlier slot is impossible. More generally, fix a slot $r$. After any feasible reordering confined strictly after $r$, a feasible exchange of a job at $r$ with a better-priority job at a later slot is still impossible.

Fix a normalized full schedule of a domain and let $S$ and $S^+$ be consecutive priority prefixes, differing by the promotion of one job from high to low. Suppose $s$ is a separator at cutoff $S$, either inside the domain or at its exterior left boundary. Then there is a separator $t\ge s$, found by advancing only to domain slots on the right, that separates both $S$ and $S^+$. If the priority order is specified on a larger job set and the promoted job is outside the domain, one may take $t=s$.
Every ideal of a nonempty set with a full schedule has an actual separator in some full schedule of that set.

Let a list be pruned on $W'$. Suppose $x\in W'$ qualifies and $y$ is any global qualifier of the pruned list. If the pruned key of $x$ is smaller than the pruned key of $y$, the same comparison held before pruning.
Every pruned list produced by this construction has at most five entries. At most three of them are injections from its current run.

Consider an already constructed edge from a parent $U$ to a child $W$, in its old working frame. Its low cutoff $H_-\subseteq U$ has a global downset extension $H_-^*$ agreeing with it on $U$. This extension can be chosen with at most $21$ leaves.
Every entry constructed above has fewer than $40$ leaves. This bound persists through any number of same-direction updates.

Every marked slot $z$ in a node $W$ has a bounded relative description of its earlier jobs in either the working direction that produced it or the original direction. The formulas use the stated atomic language and have fewer than $500$ leaves, as counted in [lem:final-count](#lem:final-count).
The predicates in [lem:global-child](#lem:global-child), [lem:relative-splits](#lem:relative-splits) have fewer than $500$ leaves.

purpose: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Three-Machine Unit-Job Scheduling

coverage.checked_domain: All DAGs with edges increasing in identifier for 1 <= n <= 4, every 1 <= T <= n; plus explicit boundary and reversed-label DAGs up to n=6. This covers all DAGs up to relabeling in the exhaustive range.
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent exhaustive enumeration of all T^n slot assignments, integer capacity checks, strict arc checks and exact rechecking of every returned schedule. No solver is used. No coverage of bounded-description hierarchy or asymptotic running time.

title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Three-Machine Unit-Job Scheduling
